drugRefs.regimenLabel: Penicillin V (only if GAS confirmed or very high pretest probability)
drugRefs.why: Penicillin remains first-line for confirmed Group A Streptococcal pharyngitis - narrow spectrum, no resistance reported, and prevents rheumatic fever when given for a full 10-day course.

refs: IDSA Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis Guidelines

coverageMatrix.completeness: Penicillin provides complete coverage of confirmed GAS pharyngitis.
gaps: No coverage needed for viral causes - antibiotics provide no benefit there.

stewardship.deescalation: If RADT/culture is negative, discontinue any antibiotics started and manage symptomatically. If positive, continue the targeted penicillin-class regimen for the full duration to prevent rheumatic fever.

drugs.why: Penicillin remains first-line for confirmed Group A Streptococcal pharyngitis - narrow spectrum, no resistance reported, and prevents rheumatic fever when given for a full 10-day course.

drugs.coverage: Equally effective alternative to penicillin V with better palatability, especially in children.
Reserved for confirmed penicillin allergy; rising macrolide resistance in some regions should be considered.

framework: Do not treat empirically without testing unless Centor score is high (≥3) and rapid testing is unavailable.
A negative rapid strep test in a low-to-moderate pretest probability patient should not be treated with antibiotics.
Avoid azithromycin as a default first choice - reserve for confirmed penicillin allergy.
